english: Let $T$ be the set of all real numbers $t$ for which the principal argument of $(1+it)^{3}$ is $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the sum of the values of $\dfrac{2t}{1+t^{2}}$ over all $t\in T$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $T$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $t$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $(1+it)^{3}$ का मुख्य कोणांक $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ है, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। तब सभी $t\in T$ पर $\dfrac{2t}{1+t^{2}}$ के मानों का योग ______ है।
solution: Put $t=\tan\theta$, $\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$: $1+it=\sec\theta\,e^{i\theta}$, so by De Moivre $(1+it)^{3}=\sec^{3}\theta\,e^{3i\theta}$ with $\sec\theta>0$
$\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ ($t=1$) or $\theta=-\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$ ($t=-2-\sqrt{3}$); the third root $t=-2+\sqrt{3}$ of $\tan3\theta=-1$ gives argument $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and is rejected
solution_full: Every real $t$ is $\tan\theta$ for a unique $\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, and $1+i\tan\theta=\sec\theta(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)$ with $\sec\theta>0$.
By De Moivre's theorem, $(1+it)^{3}=\sec^{3}\theta(\cos3\theta+i\sin3\theta)$, so an argument of $(1+it)^{3}$ is $3\theta$, where $3\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$.

The principal argument is $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ exactly when $3\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+2k\pi$ for an integer $k$. In the interval this allows $3\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ ($k=0$) and $3\theta=-\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ ($k=-1$).

Algebraic check: $(1+it)^{3}=(1-3t^{2})+i(3t-t^{3})$. Argument $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ needs $3t-t^{3}=-(1-3t^{2})>0$, i.e. $t^{3}+3t^{2}-3t-1=0$, $(t-1)(t^{2}+4t+1)=0$, $t=1,-2\pm\sqrt{3}$. For $t=-2+\sqrt{3}$, $1-3t^{2}>0$, so the argument is $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and this root is rejected; $t=1$ and $t=-2-\sqrt{3}$ give real part $<0$ and imaginary part $>0$, as required.
originality_note: New: the principal-argument condition on (1+it)^3 selects two of the three roots of tan 3theta = -1, because 3 arctan t ranges over (-3pi/2, 3pi/2) (way 5, the branch selection is the discovery). Closest known: tan 3theta formula through (1 + i tan theta)^3 by De Moivre. Different because: a principal-argument condition rather than tan 3theta is given, so one algebraic root is extraneous and two branches survive.

concept_use.De Moivre theorem: (sec theta e^{i theta})^3 = sec^3 theta e^{3i theta} gives the argument 3theta of (1+it)^3.
concept_use.Multiple angles: ratios of 2A and 3A: tan 3theta = -1 (equivalently (3t - t^3)/(1-3t^2)) gives the candidates, and 2t/(1+t^2) = sin 2theta evaluates the sum.

key_step: Write t = tan theta, use De Moivre so arg = 3theta in (-3pi/2, 3pi/2), keep the two admissible branches and reject t = -2+sqrt3.
justification: Two linked ideas (De Moivre with principal-argument branches, multiple-angle identity) with an extraneous root that a careless solver keeps; average Advanced, like 2025-P2-Q3 (L3, branch care with inverse trig).
